stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, boosting its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, with the Department of Defense driving interest. As military contracts become a lifeline, True Anomaly's growth may be less about innovation and more about strategic timing.
stories.soWhat: This funding underscores the shift towards defense-centric space solutions, where funding isn't just about technology but survival in a crowded market.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team for tactical SDA constellation
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have partnered to bid on a tactical Space Development Agency constellation, highlighting the increasing importance of collaboration in defense contracting. The push for a more integrated approach to space operations reflects a broader trend in defense procurement. In a world where solo acts fade, teamwork is the new rock star.
stories.soWhat: This collaboration signals that the future of space defense will rely heavily on partnerships, not lone wolves, to meet complex operational demands.

stories.head: Germany advocates for European military space command
stories.body: Germany is pushing for a European military space command to enhance operational efficiency, signaling a potential shift in the continent's approach to defense. This initiative aims to streamline operations and could lead to a unified strategy among EU nations. If successful, it might finally make the European space sector less of a patchwork quilt and more of a cohesive unit.
stories.soWhat: This move could reshape the European defense landscape, but it also raises questions about national sovereignty and collaboration—who will really play nice?

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's progress
watchlist.body: With $190M in new funding, True Anomaly's next steps could influence the co-orbital security landscape significantly.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.

tickers.note: SpaceX's secondary market valuation has hit $470B, making it a prime example of how hype can inflate valuations.
Palantir's recent $480M extension on the TITAN program shows that some contracts mature into valuable assets.
True Anomaly's $190M Series C funding illustrates that cash flow often trumps actual technological innovation.
The bullish case for ASTS suggests execution risk is the only hurdle left, which is either a blessing or a curse.
